definitions.explanation: The state of not wearing shoes or socks, with feet directly touching the ground.
Used in the pattern 〜も{裸足|はだし}で{逃|に}げる to mean someone is so skilled that even a professional would run away barefoot in defeat.

examples.japanese: {裸足|はだし}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{歩|ある}く→歩く：00538_aruku⟧。
{子|こ}どもたち⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{裸足|はだし}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{砂浜|すなはま}→砂浜：12333_sunahama⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{走|はし}り{回|まわ}った→走り回る：04608_hashirimawaru⟧。
examples.english: The children ran around barefoot on the sandy beach.
It feels good to walk barefoot on the grass.

examples.japanese: ⟦プロ→プロ：03871_puro⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧{裸足|はだし}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{逃|に}げる→逃げる：01151_nigeru⟧⟦{腕前|うでまえ}→腕前：07299_udemae⟧だ。
examples.english: His skill is so great that even professionals would run away barefoot.

examples.japanese: ⟦{彼女|かのじょ}→彼女：01286_kanojo⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{料理|りょうり}→料理：01523_ryouri⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧、⟦シェフ→シェフ：05062_shefu⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧{裸足|はだし}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{逃|に}げる→逃げる：01151_nigeru⟧ほどだ。
examples.english: Her cooking is so good that even chefs would run away barefoot.

examples.japanese: ⟦{素人|しろうと}→素人：04270_shirouto⟧な⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{玄人|くろうと}→玄人：09079_kurouto⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧{裸足|はだし}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{出来|でき}→出来：11763_deki⟧だった。
examples.english: Although an amateur, the result would put professionals to shame.

notes:
USAGE:
Also written as {素足|はだし} or はだし in kana. In Japan, going barefoot indoors (after removing slippers) is common in traditional settings, but going barefoot outdoors has the same connotations as in Western cultures.

The figurative expression 〜⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧{裸足|はだし}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{逃|に}げる→逃げる：01151_nigeru⟧ (even ~ would run away barefoot) is an idiom meaning someone is so skilled that professionals would flee in defeat.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {裸足|はだし}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{歩|ある}く→歩く：00538_aruku⟧ (to walk barefoot)
- {裸足|はだし}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{走|はし}る→走る：00519_hashiru⟧ (to run barefoot)
- {裸足|はだし}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{逃|に}げる→逃げる：01151_nigeru⟧ (to run away barefoot — figurative for being outclassed)
